threads.title: Take the recruiter's offer or stay?
threads.problem: A perception role elsewhere pays forty percent more; the work is maintenance of a mature system.

steps.text: A perception role elsewhere pays forty percent more; the work is maintenance of a mature system.
What do you know for certain about the day-to-day of each job, as opposed to what you imagine?
Here: I decide what to build and fix my own mistakes. There: the roadmap is set, the system works, the pay is better.
If money were equal, which option would you be explaining to a friend with more energy?
What will you decide, and what is the one sentence you would give the recruiter?
Staying. I would rather build the second arm slowly than maintain someone else's first one.

outcome.summary: The pay difference is real; the work difference is bigger. Revisit in six months if the plan slips.

items.text: Entries that mention sleep average a full point below the rest; the earplugs week is the exception.
Running days are the best-rated days, but they are also the days with the most other activity, so the direction of cause is open.
The Sunday dip is consistent across six Sundays; it is a weekly rhythm, not an event.

data.state: Eight weeks in, the journal shows a demo crunch in the middle, a recovery driven by running and the side project, and a sleep debt that keeps coming back through the neighbours and the early recordings. The career question is settled; the sleep question is not.

in_play.reading: Distance up and knee quiet since the physio routine.
Better after the earplugs, undercut by the dawn recordings.
Daily practice is real now that an exam date exists.

heads_up.text: Three of the last seven entries were written after 22:30 with energy at 2 or below.

forecast.text: If the dawn recordings continue three mornings a week, expect another low-energy stretch within a fortnight.
